item.title: Oil Rises After Trump Says the US Doesn’t Need a Deal With Iran
item.description: Oil rose after President Donald Trump said that the US doesn’t need a deal with Iran, dimming prospects for a breakthrough to end the war that has roiled Middle East supplies.

item.title: Paraguay on Watch for Downgrade at Fitch After Bank Collapse
item.description: Paraguay’s new government said it’s working to shore up its financial system after Fitch Ratings placed its credit rating on watch for a potential downgrade, citing risks from a banking crisis that toppled President Santiago Peña and rattled investors.

item.title: At Hyperliquid, Traders Bid for Edge in Crypto’s High-Speed Race
item.description: Crypto trading firm Wintermute has become a prominent user of a system that allows traders to pay for early access to data on Hyperliquid, giving them a head start over rivals on one of the world’s largest decentralized derivatives exchanges.

item.title: US Utilities Have a Plan to Win Over the AI Haters
item.description: Power companies say they’re working to ensure data centers pay up to connect to the grid, but widespread skepticism persists.

item.title: Nvidia Sinks as Analyst Downgrades Start to Come In: Street Wrap
item.description: Nvidia Corp. shares fall as much as 8.4% in premarket trading following reports the AI chipmaker’s board is working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang. The move follows reports of extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy. If the premarket losses hold, the stock is set to drop below $4 trillion in market capitalization when cash trading resumes.
